newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver sag, seasonal demand subdued.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver sag, seasonal demand subdued.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 15 rupees lower at 4,795 per 10 grammes against Saturday's close of 4,810 rupees. Sluggish seasonal demand and weaker world markets dragged local prices lower. Gold gained 15 rupees on Saturday.

** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 200 rupees lower at 56,100 per piece against Saturday's close of 56,300 rupees. Biscuits gained 200 rupees on Saturday, and 400 rupees during last week.

** Silver (.999) closed 40 rupees lower at 6,960 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,000 rupees on the back of higher arrivals of the imported silver while subdued trend on world markets kept industrial buyers away. Silver was down by 25 rupees per kg on Saturday.

Gold 24 carat closed 15 rupees lower at 4,795 rupees per 10 grammes compared to Saturday's close as seasonal buying pittered out at the higher level while losses in the world market triggered profit-taking, dealer said.
Gold was up by 15 rupees per 10 gramme on Saturday and by 35 rupees during last week.
Meanwhile, prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 200 rupees lower at 56,100 rupees per piece, reversing a 200 rupee gain on Saturday. Biscuits gained 400 rupees per piece last week.
Arrivals of the imported gold remained low but sentiment at the close was subdued as traders expected a resumption of sales of confiscated gold by the customs department.
Silver (.999) closed 40 rupees lower at 6,960 rupees per kg as increased arrivals of imports conspired with sliding world prices and industrial buyers stood back from the market.
Silver fell 25 rupees per kg on Saturday and by 40 rupees last week.
Arrivals of imported silver in Bombay remained low in the early trade but picked up thereafter during the day totalling about 1,000/1,500 kg towards the close. ($1=35.84 rupees)
